about: Authored query pairs on Oracle Customer Orders for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the CO data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates. Upstream's UNIQUE constraints cannot be declared in BigQuery DDL and are dropped, so pairs that would need them are labelled different.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: orders.customer_id is NOT NULL and references customers' key
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_status FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, order_status FROM orders

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: order_items.shipment_id may be NULL: an item not yet shipped joins no shipment (1,238 of the 3,914 real items)
pairs.left: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id FROM order_items AS oi JOIN shipments AS s ON oi.shipment_id = s.shipment_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key an order may name a customer that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_status FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, order_status FROM orders

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without customers' primary key two customers may share an id and the order joins both
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_status FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, order_status FROM orders

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: order_items.order_id is NOT NULL and references orders' key
pairs.left: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key an item may belong to an order that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a LEFT JOIN on the key of stores adds no row and no filter
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id FROM orders

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a customer appears once per order
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id FROM customers

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without stores' primary key a store id may repeat
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id FROM orders

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a self join on the whole composite key (order_id, line_item_id) matches each row with itself
pairs.left: SELECT a.order_id, a.line_item_id, a.quantity FROM order_items AS a JOIN order_items AS b ON a.order_id = b.order_id AND a.line_item_id = b.line_item_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id, quantity FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: order_id alone is not the key: an order with several items matches each item with all of them
pairs.left: SELECT a.order_id, a.line_item_id, a.quantity FROM order_items AS a JOIN order_items AS b ON a.order_id = b.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id, quantity FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two items may be identical and match each other
pairs.left: SELECT a.order_id, a.line_item_id, a.quantity FROM order_items AS a JOIN order_items AS b ON a.order_id = b.order_id AND a.line_item_id = b.line_item_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id, quantity FROM order_items

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the join keeps exactly the items whose shipment_id is not NULL (foreign key to the key of shipments)
pairs.left: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id FROM order_items AS oi JOIN shipments AS s ON s.shipment_id = oi.shipment_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items WHERE shipment_id IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a shipment_id may name no shipment
pairs.left: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id FROM order_items AS oi JOIN shipments AS s ON s.shipment_id = oi.shipment_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items WHERE shipment_id IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a self join on the primary key
pairs.left: SELECT a.product_id, a.product_name FROM products AS a JOIN products AS b ON a.product_id = b.product_id
pairs.right: SELECT product_id, product_name FROM products

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key a product row may repeat
pairs.left: SELECT a.product_id, a.product_name FROM products AS a JOIN products AS b ON a.product_id = b.product_id
pairs.right: SELECT product_id, product_name FROM products

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: customer_id is the primary key
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, full_name FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, full_name FROM customers

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a customer places many orders
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id FROM orders

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two customer rows may be identical
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, full_name FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, full_name FROM customers

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: (order_id, line_item_id) is the primary key
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: upstream makes (product_id, order_id) UNIQUE, which BigQuery cannot declare and this eval drops: under the declared keys an order may list a product on two lines (the real data has none, so the pair agrees on it)
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT order_id, product_id FROM order_items
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, product_id FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key an item row may repeat
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: upstream declares UNIQUE (email_address), which BigQuery cannot declare and this eval drops: under the declared keys two customers may share an email (the real data has none)
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT email_address FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT email_address FROM customers

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: IN over a subquery is EXISTS of the correlated subquery
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'REFUNDED')
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'REFUNDED')

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the subquery selects orders.customer_id, which repeats: the join gives one row per refunded order
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'REFUNDED'
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'REFUNDED')

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the subquery selects customers' primary key, so the join cannot repeat an order
pairs.left: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE full_name = 'Walter Rogers')
pairs.right: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.full_name = 'Walter Rogers'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without customers' primary key two customers may share an id and the join repeats the order
pairs.left: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE full_name = 'Walter Rogers')
pairs.right: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.full_name = 'Walter Rogers'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: order_items.product_id is NOT NULL, so NOT IN cannot be poisoned by a NULL
pairs.left: SELECT product_id FROM products WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)
pairs.right: SELECT p.product_id FROM products AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: order_items.shipment_id has NULLs: NOT IN then returns no row at all (the NOT EXISTS form returns the 7 shipments no item uses)
pairs.left: SELECT shipment_id FROM shipments WHERE shipment_id NOT IN (SELECT shipment_id FROM order_items)
pairs.right: SELECT s.shipment_id FROM shipments AS s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS oi WHERE oi.shipment_id = s.shipment_id)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without NOT NULL on order_items.product_id one NULL makes NOT IN return nothing
pairs.left: SELECT product_id FROM products WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)
pairs.right: SELECT p.product_id FROM products AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: product_name is NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COALESCE(product_name, 'none') AS n FROM products
pairs.right: SELECT product_name AS n FROM products

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: products.unit_price may be NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COALESCE(unit_price, 0) AS p FROM products
pairs.right: SELECT unit_price AS p FROM products

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: order_tms is NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE order_tms IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT order_id FROM orders

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: only the online store has a web address
pairs.left: SELECT store_id FROM stores WHERE web_address IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT store_id FROM stores

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: email_address is NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(email_address) FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: 1,238 items have no shipment
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(shipment_id) FROM order_items
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_items

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: email_address depends on the grouped primary key customer_id
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.email_address
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two customer rows may share id and name but differ in email
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.email_address
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: store_id is not determined by customer_id
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id, store_id
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: product_id depends on the composite primary key (order_id, line_item_id)
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, line_item_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id, line_item_id, product_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id, line_item_id

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the key the same (order, line) may appear with two products
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, line_item_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id, line_item_id, product_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id, line_item_id

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a HAVING on the group key is a WHERE
pairs.left: SELECT order_status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY order_status HAVING order_status <> 'OPEN'
pairs.right: SELECT order_status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE order_status <> 'OPEN' GROUP BY order_status

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a store with no completed order has no group on the left and a zero on the right
pairs.left: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETE' GROUP BY store_id
pairs.right: SELECT store_id, COUNTIF(order_status = 'COMPLETE') AS n FROM orders GROUP BY store_id

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the same status appears many times
pairs.left: SELECT order_status AS s FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT shipment_status AS s FROM shipments
pairs.right: SELECT order_status AS s FROM orders UNION DISTINCT SELECT shipment_status AS s FROM shipments

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the two filters split a NOT NULL column into two disjoint halves
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items WHERE quantity > 2 UNION ALL SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items WHERE quantity <= 2
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, line_item_id FROM order_items

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: unit_price may be NULL and then matches neither half
pairs.left: SELECT product_id FROM products WHERE unit_price > 20 UNION ALL SELECT product_id FROM products WHERE unit_price <= 20
pairs.right: SELECT product_id FROM products

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both customer_id columns are NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM orders INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT customer_id FROM shipments
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM shipments)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: INTERSECT matches NULLs, IN does not (1,238 real items have a NULL shipment)
pairs.left: SELECT shipment_id FROM order_items INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT shipment_id FROM order_items
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT shipment_id FROM order_items WHERE shipment_id IN (SELECT shipment_id FROM order_items)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the filter on the outer side rejects the NULL-padded rows
pairs.left: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id, s.shipment_status FROM order_items AS oi LEFT JOIN shipments AS s ON oi.shipment_id = s.shipment_id WHERE s.shipment_status = 'DELIVERED'
pairs.right: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id, s.shipment_status FROM order_items AS oi JOIN shipments AS s ON oi.shipment_id = s.shipment_id WHERE s.shipment_status = 'DELIVERED'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the filter accepts the NULL-padded row of an unshipped item
pairs.left: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id, s.shipment_status FROM order_items AS oi LEFT JOIN shipments AS s ON oi.shipment_id = s.shipment_id WHERE s.shipment_status IS NULL OR s.shipment_status = 'DELIVERED'
pairs.right: SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id, s.shipment_status FROM order_items AS oi JOIN shipments AS s ON oi.shipment_id = s.shipment_id WHERE s.shipment_status IS NULL OR s.shipment_status = 'DELIVERED'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the partition key keeps whole partitions
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, customer_id, r FROM (SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_status, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_tms) AS r FROM orders) AS t WHERE customer_id = 5
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, customer_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_tms) AS r FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 5

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: filtering before the window changes the ranks
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, customer_id, r FROM (SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_status, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_tms) AS r FROM orders) AS t WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETE'
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, customer_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_tms) AS r FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETE'
